newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says it will help returning Kurds.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says it will help returning Kurds.

text.p: Turkey said on Thursday that it would provide financial aid to its citizens returning from a United Nations-sponsored Kurdish refugee camp in northern Iraq and gave assurances for their safety.

"Our government is determined to make all attempts for all our citizens who will return to Turkey to provide a secure and peaceful life...the returning families' security will be a priority," a Turkish foreign ministry statement said.
Turkey has long sought the camp's closure, charging that it was a base for operations by the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK), whose rebels are fighting for self-rule in southeast Turkey.
The U.N. refugee agency UNHCR said earlier this month it would pull out from the Atrush camp because its work was blocked by "activists" preventing refugees from going home.
Atrush, 60 km (38 miles) from the Turkish border has been home since 1994 to some 14,000 Turkish Kurds fleeing the conflict in southeast Turkey.
The statement said returnees would get financial aid to build or restore their homes, along with food and healthcare.
